questions.q: Why is the security review checklist organized by attack category (injection, poisoning, extraction, adversarial, architecture) instead of one general 'is this secure?' question?
options: Categories are only used for documentation purposes and don't affect the review outcome
Attack categories are unrelated to each other, so grouping them has no benefit
A general question skips checkable, category-specific items that a focused checklist catches
A general question is always sufficient and categories just add paperwork
questions.explain: Organizing by category, drawn from the six earlier chapters, surfaces specific checkable gaps that a vague general review tends to miss.

questions.q: In Category 1, what does marking retrieved content as 'data' in the prompt template, rather than concatenating it as instructions, actually prevent?
options: It prevents the retriever from working at all
It has no real effect on the feature's behavior
It only matters for help-center articles, never for ticket text
It prevents the model from treating untrusted retrieved text as a command it should follow
questions.explain: This is the direct fix for Lesson 29's finding -- it stops retrieved content from being interpreted as an instruction from the user.

questions.q: What does Category 5's 'privilege separation' requirement mean for close_ticket and issue_refund?
options: They should be combined into a single tool for efficiency
They run as distinct, narrowly-scoped tools so a summarization call can't also trigger a refund
They should both be removed from the feature entirely
Privilege separation only applies to human employees, not AI tools
questions.explain: Narrowly scoping each tool means no single compromised or manipulated call can reach a sensitive action it wasn't meant to reach.

questions.q: Why does the go/no-go gate require issue_refund to pass BOTH the Category 1 injection fix AND the Category 5 human approval gate before shipping?
options: A checklist that catches the injection but still lets the agent refund money autonomously hasn't actually closed the risk -- both conditions have to be true
Only one of the two categories is ever actually relevant to a refund tool
The approval gate alone is always sufficient on its own
The injection fix alone is always sufficient on its own
questions.explain: Closing only one gap leaves the other path to an unintended refund open, so the gate treats both as required, not optional alternatives.

questions.q: According to Category 5, where should secrets used by a tool like issue_refund be exposed?
options: Directly to the model's prompt context so it can use them
Never to the model itself -- only to the code invoking the tool
In the retrieved ticket content for convenience
In the chapter 1 OWASP checklist document
questions.explain: Keeping secrets out of the model's context means a successful injection still can't exfiltrate credentials the model never saw.
